utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I promised yesterday to let you know about next week Friday. We will not sit next week Friday, and early next week the Chamber will issue an order as to how the Fridays will be utilised. Is it Mr. Docherty to call the new witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Your Honours, the Prosecution calls Sabina Sabanic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Could you begin, please, by telling us your name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: My name is Sabina Sabanic. I was born on the 3rd of January, 1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm going to talk to you about a couple of statements that you gave to investigators from this Tribunal. First of all, did you speak with an investigator from the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia on 16 November of 1995?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Since coming to The Hague a few days ago to testify, have you had the opportunity to read that statement over carefully?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In what language did you read that statement?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: In Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, I understand that you have a couple of directions to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, I beg your pardon for interrupting. Your microphone is on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I was going to say, Witness, that you have a couple of corrections to make to that statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And the first one concerns the time at which you left work on the day that you were shot. What would be the correct time at which you left work on the day that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: The exact time when I left work was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please repeat the time. It wasn't heard, the time when you left work.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was around ten or five to 4.00 on that day when I left work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I understand there is a second correction which concerns the first aid or medical attention that you received from some UNPROFOR soldiers. In the statement it says that they bandaged your wound. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: No. They gave me oxygen in their vehicle because I was losing consciousness, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: With those two corrections made, is the statement of 16 November 1995 true and correct?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender into evidence the witness's statement of 16 November 1995. The 65 ter number is 2890.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P153.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I neglected to mention earlier but should have: This witness will be giving evidence pursuant to 92 ter, and this testimony will concern scheduled sniping incident number 8 to the amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, did you also speak to another investigator from this Tribunal on the 22nd of May, 1996?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And, again, since coming to The Hague to testify, have you had an opportunity to read that statement over carefully?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In what language did you read it?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: In Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I understand you to have one correction to make concerning that statement which has to do with your child's reaction to certain movies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And what would that correction be? What is your child's reaction to movies with themes of war or shooting or things like that?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I think my child reacts like every other teenager. I wouldn't say that my child is avoiding watching these kinds of films.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Once that correction is made, ma'am, is the statement of 22nd of May, 2006, true and correct?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender the witness's statement of 22 May 2006. The 65 ter number is 2891.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P154.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, what was the date on which you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: 23 November 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What were you doing when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I was driving -- I was in the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask for an aerial photograph to be put on the monitor in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if I could please ask the court officer to pull up 65 ter number 2819.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, it will take a moment or two for that to come up. But while we are waiting, let me direct you to a statement in your statement of 16 November 1995 where you say that: "There was panic all over the tram." Do you remember that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What was it that you saw that day, what was it that you heard that that day, and what observations did you make that led you to the conclusion that there was "panic all over the tram"?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Panic reigned or set in at the time when people were getting wounded, covered in blood, and of course that's when panic set in. Everybody wanted to get off; however, it was not safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The photograph is now up on the monitor in front of you. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the scene in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if I could ask the usher's assistance, I'm going to ask the witness to use the SMART Board to make some markings on this photograph. Before we begin marking on this photograph, Your Honour, I'll tender the unmarked photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is already an exhibit, number P88.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Then I will not seek to tender it, Your Honour. Thank you for the correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, on this photograph, could you just draw a line with an arrow showing us the direction that the tram you were in was travelling on the day you were shot.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you mark with an X the location of the tram when, in your words, "panic set in"?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Once --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour and Mr. Prosecutor. I have a problem. I'm trying to follow the transcript on my screen, but it's not working. It's very hard to follow what's on the photograph and the transcript. If something could be done, because my screen is not working for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm told that they are aware of the problem and they're working on it. But you are receiving the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. But it's easier when you also have the transcript to see if this is exactly what the witness is saying and to be able to check things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that. Well, we expect that that will be corrected shortly, so continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you see on --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Excuse me. I wanted to ask a different question first, and I'm going to ask this question, Mr. Usher, and ask for an another marking and then I will be done with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Court the physical sensation you experienced upon being shot on the 23rd of November, 1994?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Well, when a person gets shot or wounded, you don't feel the pain immediately. When people said in the tram that there was shooting, there were lots of injured people. There was one wounded people -- person behind me, and I thought that he was, or she, the only one who was wounded because I didn't hear anything. When the tram stopped, everyone got off in panic. I was feeling very bad. I was losing consciousness, and I ascribe this to fear and panic that I felt at the time. However, I was injured, after all. I couldn't move my arm. It was November. I had my coat on, a blazer, but I saw blood on my arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And looking at the photograph in front of you, do you see the spot where you realised you had been shot on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You've marked the spot where, in your words, "panic set in"; correct?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: After you realised that panic had set in, what did the tram do?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: The tram continued travelling because that was an unsafe area, and it went behind this other building - that's the museum - and that is where we got off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this point I'm going to tender the marked photograph that is on the monitor and then switch to a different photograph that I believe will be more helpful for the balance of the witness's testimony. So at this time I tender the marked photograph on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P155.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if I might, please, ask the court officer -- I'm sorry, I'll wait a moment. Mr. Usher, I will be through marking for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do we have it yet? No? It's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If I can ask the court officer, then, to call up a different aerial photograph. It's got 65 ter number 2906. And while that is being done, I can continue my examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly ask the witness's microphones to be adjusted because the witness is barely audible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour, I really suffer from the fact that I cannot read the transcript. I don't have this exhibit number on the 65 ter list. I don't know if there's been a mistake in the number of the exhibit, because I don't have the transcript to check it out. I cannot check whether it's 2909, did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The number is 65 ter number is 2906. It was disclosed to the Defence in hard copy following court a couple of days ago. It is an aerial photograph and it is on the monitor at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's on the monitor, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photograph that is on the monitor in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, just so that we can orient ourselves with respect to the photograph that was here before, do you see on the photograph that's there now something called the Marshal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, before the witness marks, I will ask that this photograph be introduced into evidence in its unmarked condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P156.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, can you ask the witness to show us where these Marshal Tito barracks are, because I was unable to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I was just about to, Your Honour. I just wanted to admit it before we started marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, could you please draw a square or a rectangle around the perimeter of the Marshal Tito barracks.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: This is this part, but there's something else, because something is being worked on here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And can you just draw for us the part that's being worked on. Could you outline that as well, please.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And on the previous photograph I asked you to make an X at the spot where panic set in on the tram. Is that spot also on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And just so we can orient ourselves and move easily from one photograph to the other, could you make that X on this photograph as well, please, in the same spot that it was on in the last photograph.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you have an opinion, Witness, as to where the bullets came from -- the bullet, excuse me, came from that hit you on the 23rd of November, 1994?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that opinion is and also the reasons why you have that opinion.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: There was shooting in Sarajevo. The most difficult thing was to cross this part here, this one here. The shots were always coming from these three sky-scrapers that were held by the Serb army, or whatever they were called. Even when the tram was not operating, it was difficult. We used to use this part here to walk through, and it was very difficult to cross this section. We had to run.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to make a couple of more marks on there. You said "these three" buildings here, and so we know which three buildings, can you put a tick mark, a check mark on each of those three buildings.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you, beside the two rectangles that you wrote for the Marshal Tito barracks, put the letter -- capital letter T, for "Tito."

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And could you, beside the line that you indicate was the safer way to go, put the capital letter S for the English word "safer"?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: You mean after you've crossed this section, that it was safer? Are you referring to this part of the route?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: No. On the photograph you have made a mark - do you see it? - which is not labelled yet. It is a line. And you said, I believe, that that was a safer way to go but that you still had to run. Do you recall the -- and I apologise, I don't have a transcript in front of me so I can't quote you exactly. But do you remember the testimony I'm referring to? And do you see that line, that red line, on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: No. I said that in the period when we had to walk to this line, this is where we walked. This section was also difficult to cross because of snipers. We had to run across.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, before this is removed from the screen, I wanted to get back to the question you asked her as to the reason why she held the opinion that the shots came from a particular direction, and her answer was that the shots were always coming from these three sky-scrapers that were held by the Serb army. So I presume she -- Am I right in then saying that your opinion is that the shots were coming from the three sky-scrapers held by the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. But your reason for saying that is that in the past that's where the shots always came from. Is your only reason for saying that because the shots always came from that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in the tram facing Grbavica, facing that area where those buildings are. A bullet hit me on this side; it was a direct hit. So it is for those reasons that I believe that it came from there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Again, we must draw everyone's attention to the fact that the witness is not speaking into the microphone and she is barely audible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it possible to have the second microphone placed in front of her? Well, I'm clearer now as to the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. President. Now we have no interpretation and no transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter in the French booth apologises; she was on the wrong channel. The French translation is back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The French translation is back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, the line that you were marking just before you and Judge Robinson had a conversation, could you mark that with a W for the English word "walk"?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour. Could I have what you have just said, the exchange of words between Your Honour and the witness. I don't have the translation and maybe I can try and find it on the transcript. It's very important, as far as I'm concerned. I don't have the transcript. I have got the photograph on the screen and it's very difficult for me to switch all the time. I don't know what is being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'll repeat. I asked the witness whether the only reason for her saying that the shots came from the three sky-scrapers is that in the past that was where the shots came from. And then she replied: "I was in the tram facing ... the area where those buildings are. A bullet hit me on this side; it was a direct hit. So it is for those reasons that I believe that it came from there." And I then said that I was clearer as to her reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, the line on the photograph that we've been talking about, can you please mark that with a capital W for the English word "walk." The route that you would take, that you have marked with a red mark, for when you had to walk rather than take the tram.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: This is where one walked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender the marked-up photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P157.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, what was the weather like on the 23rd of November, 1994, the day that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: It was rather cold. No precipitation, though. Clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You said that you had left work about ten to 4.00, maybe five to 4.00. How long did it then take the tram to get to the place where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: The tram would normally reach that stop at about 4.00. That was the stop where I was usually waiting. Since this was the last tram to run on that particular day, it was awfully crowded. Whenever trams were running, all those on their way to work used them rather than to walk. I don't know how long it takes exactly. Each of the stops were awfully crowded, which implied that the tram would wait at each of the stops every time, probably longer than usual under the circumstances that prevailed. But I can't tell you exactly how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. In any event, in late November in Sarajevo, what time does the sun go down, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: About 5.00. In November it would about 5.00. Perhaps even slightly sooner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And can you tell us how much light was left at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: When I was shot, there was still natural light. It wasn't entirely dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers in the area where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Was there any combat going on, fighting between the two armies going on, at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: No, there wasn't. It was, as a matter of fact, quite a peaceful day in comparison. We were even using the trams.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And a few minutes ago - and this is the end of my direction examination - you showed Judge Robinson where the bullet had hit you. For clarity of the record, could you point on your body to the place where the bullet entered.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: The bullet entered here and exited back here, like this. This is where it entered and this is where it exited.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And for the purposes of the record, Mr. President, may the record reflect that the witness has pointed to her right shoulder, an inch or two below the top, and has indicates that the bullet entered at the front; and that the witness then indicated a corresponding spot on her back, about 2 inches below the top of the shoulder, and indicated that that was the place where the bullet exited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Docherty. Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good morning. I am Branislava Isailovic; I am an attorney with the Paris bar. According to the procedure that we use here, I have to ask a few questions that have to do with the statements that you made on November 16, 1995, and on May 22nd, 2006, and a few more questions that have to do with what you just said this morning in this courtroom. So, first, I would like to know if -- I would like to start with your statements. I'm sure you remember your statements. We don't have to have them on screen. Would you rather have them on screen, you know, to refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I don't think there is a need for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So, in your first statement, which was very close to the accident that occurred in 1994 - it was a statement that was made just a year after your accident - you gave some details on what really happened. You said the approximate time the incident occurred, the circumstances that were prevailing in the tram. I'm sure that you remember that.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you talked about the circumstances and you said that the windows had been broken in the tram; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: That's in the other statement. That should have been corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So if I'm right, today we talked about two statements that the Prosecutor showed you before you actually came into the courtroom. I'm sure you have read them. You've read both of them; right?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have read both. I even think that the first time, when the first statement was read, I pointed out the fact that the glass -- about the glass being shattered, and I pointed out that I'd heard no such thing as the sound of glass being shattered.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So everything is clearer now. This is not in the second statement, but today you're saying that there was no shattered glass.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Because that was amended in the second statement. That's at least what I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: It's not really the case. But you're saying it now in this hearing and we have it on the transcript, so that's fine. So regarding the place where the incident occurred - you have talked with the Prosecutor about this - is it fair to say that it happened where the tramway number 4 actually turns to go towards the station?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: No. That's between the Holiday Inn. There's a small turn where they have to switch. I'm not sure what the traffic is like there exactly. The tram just switches over a little and then it continues from the downtown area further down that route.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be useful to have the photograph that we saw earlier, and if I could ask for P88 to be put on the screen, please. It's the aerial photograph that we saw earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So on this photograph that you marked earlier, a number of elements are going to be shown. We're waiting for the photograph to be on the screen; it might take a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. If I could please ask the court officer to help the witness and to show her how to proceed in order to show us a few things on this photograph. Unfortunately, the photograph is gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May we have the photograph again?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So could you please show us this place again, the place where, according to you, the tram was hit.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Should I put an X there?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could put an X.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So that was after the intersection; right? You had already been through the intersection. And there is a curve that goes towards the station. I believe, if I remember Sarajevo right, this tram number 4 goes to the station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have a noise in the background. I'm going to ask that that be stopped.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tram number 4 goes to the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Where is the curve, please? Could you tell us where the curve is? Could you please show us where the tram takes that curve to go to the station.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I don't think you understand me. I was headed from the old town towards Batica. I wasn't going towards the railway station; I was heading straight. I couldn't even have got off at the Marshal Tito barracks if I had been on my way to the railway station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would the court deputy send a message to the person who is drilling and instruct him to stop. We can't work with that noise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm told that a check is being made and the message hopefully will be received. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I understood what direction the tramway was going. It was going straight. But this is what I'm concerned about, and I'll show you exactly what I mean: Maybe here we will see things, but we also have your statement -- we also have the statement of the tram driver. It's also a witness that we will hear soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, this is quite intolerable.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully agree with you, but I will bear through. Duty calls. But this is a really bad day. Technology is not with us at all; neither is our environment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So let's continue. We have the statement of the tram driver, and we might even hear this tram driver today.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if we could have -- if we could put on the screen the 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We cannot work with this drill which is making such a noise. The registrar must be instructed to have the drilling stopped immediately; otherwise, I will adjourn the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm told that the building is relatively big so it will take some time to locate the precise area where the drilling is so that it can be stopped. Let us see whether we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I'll ask my case manager to put on the screen number 2889 on the 65 ter list, page 3, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that statement being put on display. Counsel is certainly free to derive from that statement propositions that she wishes to put to the witness, but I do not think it proper to have all of those propositions, some of which may be agreed to or not agreed to by the witness, displayed in documentary form on the screen. I would ask counsel instead to put her case to the witness. I don't think that she needs to have the statement in front of the witness in order to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think I was entirely clear. This is a statement of a different witness. I would not object if it was this witness's statement, but this is for somebody -- this is some other witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, it's not clear to the Chamber what your reason is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: My reason is this, Your Honour: The counsel is, of course, free to put her case to the witness. She may derive the propositions she is going to put to the witness from whatever source she wishes. My objection is to having the entire statement -- the statement in question is relatively brief, to having that statement put in front of the witness and put on the screens. I believe that counsel should isolate the propositions which she wishes to put to the witness and put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is what I don't understand why. What advantage or disadvantage is there? Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me explain. This is the statement of the tram driver of this tram, who is going to be in court also. And I didn't want to tell something to the witness. I'd rather show the witness what this tram driver said. The witness will agree or disagree, but of course I will abide by your ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber rules that it may be placed before the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So if we could move to page 3 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now we are not getting it on the screen, so technology may be helping you, Mr. Docherty. It would be faulty technology. We are having a number of problems, and I was told earlier that at the break an effort will be made to resolve the problems with the technology. We appear to have succeeded as far as the drilling is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for the inconvenience, but the document is now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was there a minute ago and it just vanished; it's gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The document is on our screen on the right. Could somebody assist Ms. Isailovic, because it's on our screen. Nothing? It can't be placed on Ms. Isailovic's screen. Can it be placed on the screen of Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. It's even worse, because Mr. Tapuskovic's screen is totally dead. There's nothing. Your Honour, I have a hard copy, a good old solution that usually works. And I am not seeing exactly the same thing as you, because I have a hard copy and you have the electronic file, but I believe it's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So this tram driver is saying, when he is talking about the place where the tram was hit, he says it's the curve, he says, that goes to the news station - that's what he says in this statement - which is why I asked you that question. So could you please tell us -- show us on the photograph that place, you know, that tram that you used to go to the station, which is not your tram, but I believe it's line 4. Where does that tram actually turn? That's why I asked you that, you know, because that's the place that the tram driver indicated in his own statement. I wanted to see if you agreed with him. Because earlier we talked about the place where panic started in the tram, and I'd like to know exactly whether this corresponds or not with what was said earlier.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, this is what the driver may have had in mind. You have the tram tracks, you have the turn right there, and between the tracks - and I'm not really an expert on this - there is a switch. One switches over and the choice is between going straight ahead to the railway station or turning. So that's what the driver may have had in mind, because this is near the first museum. It's virtually opposite the technical building near the first museum. So we are now equidistant to both museums. It's just that we went off in one direction. I think that's what he may have meant.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please have the aerial photograph on the screen. On the Prosecution's list we didn't have that document, but it was shown to us -- transmitted to us here in the room, so I have it with me but without a number. If this could not happen again, please, because I don't believe that it is correct disclosure. This is not the way we communicate and disclose in the Paris bar. So I don't have the 65 ter number, but it's the photograph that we saw earlier. And it would be nice to have the 65 ter number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When was that disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It was disclosed after court on Tuesday, Your Honour. And, Your Honour, I made a mistake with the ter number. I apologise. I went from memory, which I should not do. It is it 2906.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all I have is this, but I wasn't able to make a link with any witness because there is no number to this. But this is a photograph that I was handed here in the courtroom. So could we please put this photograph on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, please, we are going to mark this photograph and then we will tender it, because there's a few things that I'm really interested in on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Court Officer, could you please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, could you please place an X at the place where you believe the tram was hit.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, earlier you said -- you talked about a green building behind which the tram took shelter after the impact. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: What I said is that the tram stopped behind the Marsal Tito barracks. I never mentioned any green building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So if you could please now show us, if you could place -- put a I above the X, the X being the place where the tram was hit. Could you also add a I, the letter I, for "impact."

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And now the place with an X where the tram actually took shelter, stopped to take shelter, from those shots.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: There were some construction works going on there and there was a building here. This is the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And could you please put an A, like "abri" in French, or shelter, above those two Xs that you marked.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that in relation to those high-rise buildings that you mentioned earlier, nothing changes when you take into account those two places?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, earlier you talked about those three high-rise buildings; do you remember that? You believe that that's the place the shots came from.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And then you said that the tram took shelter a bit further. And my question is whether, according to you, there is a difference between the first place, you know, the place where there is an A, and the other place that we marked with a I in relation to the exposure that you would get from those high-rises. Am I right in saying that it is pretty much the same situation; that the position is identical in both cases, in the I and in the A?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that I understand the question. Could you try and put it more clearly, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I'll try. I even -- while I'm reading the transcript in English, sometimes, you know, what I'm saying, I'm wondering if I'm in my right mind. So I will try to make things clearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the witness understood me - I respectfully say this - but I think she understood what I was saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph we have two locations that are marked; you agree with this? So with the I, it's the place where the impact occurred on that day, and the A is the place where, after the impact, the tram actually took shelter to be sure that it was safe and to make sure that the passengers could disembark the tram safely. My colleague asked you a question, and you showed us three high-rises located in Grbavica and from which -- you know, that place where you were hit was actually -- from which it was. So, taking into account where these two locations are compared to the high-rises, to these three high-rises, it's the same situation. The exposure in A and in I is absolutely identical; do you agree with me? Is this clear, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me see whether the witness can answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never had any weapons in my hand and I cannot say which position is easier to shoot from. But all the civilians who went through the wall, you even go into the cupboard believing that it will give you protection and shelter. This place where the tram stopped, it was practically between the buildings on each side. That is where we stood between. When you are a civilian, you can find shelter any place. You can bend down, et cetera. There were a million different situations in the war where we tried to protect ourselves, and being between these two buildings gave us a sense of security, as opposed to this place which was a clear area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, we've already dealt with these photographs earlier. Am I right if I say that in front of -- the museum was located in front of the Marshal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: No. Opposite. You can see the difference here. You can see this is where the museums are, and the second one on the right -- so between the museums, and this is where the barracks is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So will you put you a dot -- there's also a building --

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: There's the second museum there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show us this second museum, because I'm talking about the museum that can be seen on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: This one here. You can -- you can see this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my question. I know Sarajevo. Let's go back to this picture. Could you please show us Miljacka. The river Miljacka, could you show us where it flows.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: It's here, this part here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And we've heard several times in this courtroom that in that area, the Miljacka river was the border between the territory held by the BiH army and the territory held by Republika Srpska. Do you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. We didn't go across the bridges; we didn't dare do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In saying that, you're thinking only about that specific area of Grbavica, between Grbavica and Marindvor?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Pofalici as well. This whole part.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree when we say that after that -- after that area, the Miljacka is on the territory held by the BiH army. I'm thinking about Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about Hrasno? I really don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Miljacka, the river Miljacka, is separating the two warring factions in Grbavica. But further down to the west of Grbavica lies Hrasno, and Hrasno is another neighbourhood in Sarajevo. Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And in Hrasno, the line -- well, could you -- first, could you confirm by saying either yes or no, because, you know, nodding is not enough and that's not on the transcript. So to confirm you have to say something.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: No, I was just following you. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So we still agree when we say that Hrasno was a neighbourhood held by the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I really don't know where those lines and stuff were, but I know that people lived in Hrasno and used to travel to and from work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You agree with me when I say that Hrasno is adjacent to Grbavica, but on the west side.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: In fact, Hrasno borders with Grbavica. First Grbavica, then Hrasno; that's what I see in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now see something. Between the tram tracks or between road -- Zmaja od Bosne Street and Miljacka, which is the line that separates the two warring factions in Grbavica, there is a strip of land. Do you agree with me when I say that?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I don't know to which part you are referring. Everything has been changing so much in Sarajevo, so I don't know which particular part of the town you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Along the Miljacka, could you please draw a straight line, along the Miljacka.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, the entire photograph. Put an M at the beginning of that line, M like "Miljacka."

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And with a -- the street Zmaja od Bosne, could you please show us with a line that street, because that's the street that the tram took. So could you just show us the entire tram route.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: This is where the tram was travelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And put a T, maybe, on the left-hand side of the photograph to mark the tram route, please.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So now do you see what I mean in my earlier question? The strip of land that's between the Miljacka and the tram route, that's the piece of land that I was talking about. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to know if you agree with me when I say that this strip of land was controlled by the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that there were units of the BiH army who were posted in Sarajevo throughout the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I really don't know about that. Believe me, anything to do with these lines, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On this strip of land that we obtained, between those two lines, the first line being the Miljacka and the second line being the tram route, do you see fairly high buildings in that strip of land?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are they close to the place where the tram was hit?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So the high-rise that we see on that photograph, which is almost in the middle of that strip, what is that, according to you?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Do you mean this building? I think that it's a faculty building of natural sciences and mathematics.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you show us that high-rise on the screen.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: You mean this building?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one. So you said that is a faculty building. Could you put an F on it, please.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: F, as in "faculty."

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: You mean F.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And to the left there's another building that's fairly high. And what building is that, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: If you are referring to this within here, yes, I know what this building is. It's an apartment building, but there were very few people living there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Very few people that lived in that high-rise; is that what you just said?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: It was pretty much demolished. I think it was on fire at one point. People were jumping out of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you mark it with another letter on this high-rise that was burnt during the war? Maybe the letter Q in blue.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You moved around quite often during this conflict, but did you know that there was constant combat between the two warring factions in that area and that shots were fired from both sides, usually from high-rises?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I never lived in this part, no, of the town because it was enormously risky to live.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That was my question. It was extremely dangerous to live here, and there was a reason for the danger. So, according to you and according to what you heard and what was being talked about in town, wasn't it dangerous because there were always shots that were being exchanged between the two warring factions in that specific area?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I know that shots were fired from Grbavica and that there were pedestrians being fired on from this side, and this was the route that, in that period, I used to travel to and from work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, can I conclude that because you were on that side you knew about the shots that occurred and that were shot on that area, but you didn't really know what was happening on the other side and you didn't really know there were shots that were fired from the territory held by the BiH army? Could I conclude that correctly?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: You know what? When I ever I went to work and we used to run across the street, we tried to find shelter; but while I was walking around, there was no return fire. I can guarantee that for the period that I'm talking about. I cannot say about anything else. I'm talking about the period that is relevant for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I understood your answer. You said that never heard the shots that were sent as a response from the territory held by the BiH army. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I don't know if there was any fighting there. I am explaining the situation to you, as a pedestrian, as a civilian, and for the period when I had to use this route to get to work. I know that people used to run across the street and I know that we were being shot at from Grbavica. I don't know about any return fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can I conclude from this that you could make a difference between the shots fired from the north or from the south? How can you know -- make the difference between those two kinds of shots?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: I don't know what to tell you. I was facing Grbavica and the entry wound is from that direction. I don't think that the shot had come from Pofalici. I don't know what else I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, that wasn't my question. I'm not challenging the fact that you were wounded. I know you were hit on the right side. I am trying to get to something else. You're telling me that as a citizen of Sarajevo, as a person that was riding on the tram often and that was often walking in that area that we're talking about today, you heard shots, but you only heard shots that were coming from the territory held by Republika Srpska -- the army of Republika Srpska. So my question was the following: When you hear shots, are you able to make a difference, to know exactly where the shot comes from? When you hear several shots, can you make the difference? Can you know that it's only coming from one side or can you know that it's an exchange of fire? Can you make the difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: As I told you, in that period I was never caught in cross-fires; that's what I wanted to say. Secondly, while you're running down the street, when a bullet lands and when you can see where it had come from, when it hits a building, you can see where it comes from. You can always tell that and differentiate as far as that is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And can you use the sound to make that determination?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC
utterances.text: Well, what do you mean by "sound"? It has to stop somewhere. It's not like it's taking a long time to get somewhere. The bullet has to land somewhere eventually. It's not like you are watching it fly past you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One question, please, about the sound. There is the sound of the detonation and then there is also the sound of the bullet through the air. In your case, did you hear either the detonation or the sound of the bullet, or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard nothing in the tram, nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's time for the break. We'll adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I just deal with an administrative matter before we resume, and also to note that the break was extended so as to allow the technical staff to resolve the many problems that we faced with the e-court system. This morning the Prosecution filed an urgent motion for protective measures for a witness, and that witness is scheduled to testify on Monday, the 5th. This is very late because the Defence will ordinarily have two weeks in which to reply. So I'm to ask the Defence whether they are in a position to -- I'm to ask Defence whether they would be in a position to respond to the motion today so that we could rule or very early on Monday morning. Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Two things briefly, Your Honour. First, may I request a redaction of the last paragraph. It was, of course, unintentional, but counsel on the other side was unsure of the identity of the witness under discussion and said the name, at least audibly to me through the headphones - it was not caught on the transcript - but could I ask that the last, say, two minutes be redacted before going out, since it was the name of a protected the witness, or a witness for whom protection has been applied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let that be done. I'll ask all parties to be very careful in future.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It was, of course, a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We understand it was unintentional.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Secondly, Your Honour, I apologise for the tardiness of this filing. We have sought to minimise the number of these last-minute applications; I know they are irritating. All I can say is that sometimes the protective measures do not become clarified until the witness actually arrives in The Hague. We have done all we can to minimise this. I wish I could tell the Court we have reduced that to zero; I cannot make that representation, and I ask for the Court's understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let me find out whether the Defence would be in a position to reply to the motion either today or very early on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll be replying today, but I do need to know the witness's name. If that has to be done in closed session, well, so be it, but I need the name. If that's the person I have in mind, the person whose name is stated in the motion - truth to tell, I didn't even look at it this morning - we do not oppose any protective measures as a matter of principle. One thing that we can't agree on is the Prosecutor requesting any of the total measures, such as voice distortion. Whenever protective measures of this kind are requested, we do not oppose such motions, as a matter of principle. Therefore, we agree, but as long as the voice is heard, as long as there is no voice distortion. I do not oppose that. To be quite frank, I didn't read the motion yesterday. I had more urgent business. But we do not oppose that. However, should the Prosecution be requesting voice distortion as well, I submit that the decision must be for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The decision will always be the Chamber's. As far as I can see, the measures requested are pseudonym and facial distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Voice distortion is not requested with regard to this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, in light of the submissions made by the parties and the relevant provisions of the Statute and the regulations, the Chamber grants the Prosecution's application. Let us proceed with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we still have the photograph on the screen. Can you see it? We have all the markings on this photograph, and I shall now ask you to make one last marking. I would like to you indicate where the road is. You mentioned an alternative route different from the tramway, different from Zmaja od Bosne Street; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the routes that we used for walking when trams weren't running? Are those the ones you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. Could you mark this on the map, because when my colleague asked you to do so, you showed us where you crossed the road. If you could now draw a line indicating this alternative route, please.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you what the route was that I used. It's this one over here behind these buildings. One thing you must realise is there used to be a building right here at the time. So this was the risky route, and then the one you took was the one behind here and then --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We couldn't hear the last part of the witness's answer. It trailed off because one of the microphones is turned away from the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the witness to repeat the answer, because the interpreters were not able to hear it. At the same time the usher should ensure that the witness's mic is in front of her.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said is I can show the route that I took. Behind this building and then over here we would run across as fast as we could. There used to be a building here there -- there was a building standing here at the time between these buildings. So that was the route that one used.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you draw this, this building which you marked a while ago. Was this building part of the Marshal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it with a T, this building which you have already marked, please.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I've just been told that there is a T on the photograph already. Perhaps you could mark it with the letters MT and just put an M before the T, please. So this is a building which is a part of the Marshal Tito barracks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And, Witness, we have heard several witnesses talking about the "Salvation Route" or a life-saving route. Do you know something about this? At the time did you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you the question because a number of fellow citizens of yours from Sarajevo mentioned the "Salvation Road". That's what it was called at the time. And to my mind, this would be the same as what you showed us on this picture. Did you know anything about this, this "Salvation Road"? That's how it was called anyway.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, we used this route. If you think everybody else was saying the same thing, then that must be what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to continue drawing this line and show us where this road was?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an aerial view, and it has been a very long time. All these routes run between buildings, so this is not quite the way I used to see it. Some streets have been changed around and it would be very difficult for me to use this view to show you what the route was. I know it snaked between the buildings. It wasn't a straight line. There was some sort of a route passing between all of the buildings. I'm not sure that I can show you like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that there were buses that used or that went along the "Salvation Road"? Did you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Which period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the time I was wounded. I believe that's what I'm here for.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That's why you're here. But as you have been in Sarajevo for the entire time of the conflict, you're not quite sure now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I shall ask the court officer to give us an exhibit number, please, because I would like to keep this photograph with all the markings that the witness has made on it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let it be admitted and given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number D36.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like my assistant to display the aerial view, number 2818 on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, and while we're waiting for the photograph to come up on the screen, I would just like to ask you one question. Are you aware, or were you aware of a police investigation that was conducted after the tramway was hit, when you yourself were hit by a bullet?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, an investigation, I don't know about that. I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You were a victim in this incident and nobody tried to the contact you? The police never tried to contact you to take a statement?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was at the hospital and they came to the hospital to see who the wounded were. And then I was called -- and then I went for treatment and then I was called to the police station to make a statement. But I'm not familiar with any details.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Have I understood you correctly? In any case, it's been recorded in the transcript. You did say that the police came to see you when you were in hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Someone came to see us. I don't know exactly who. They came to visit the wounded, but they were not uniformed officials.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You are not quite sure, you don't know whether this person was from the police or not. The person didn't --

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was not clear at all. I made the first statement after my treatment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss what happened with other people at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Someone did come to our room to ask us how we were feeling, what sort of wounds we had suffered, that sort of thing. But you're in a state of shock. You come to the hospital and then everything is in a haze. I can't really remember who it was. That's why I'm telling you this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. I understand that you gave the wrong 65 ter number, so I'm going to ask the court deputy to give the right number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, I would like to say that this is 65 ter number 2819.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I said. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember any other victims of the tramway that were at the same hospital as you were?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was another lady in the same room as I was. Her husband had been killed and she had been wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But that was not the same victim who was with you in the same tramway; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She was in the same tram as I. We were admitted to the hospital at the same time except she arrived there differently.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you quite sure? At that time when these various people came to see you, did anybody talk to you about a bullet that had bounced back?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can now turn to the photograph which is displayed on the screen. I have asked my assistant to display this on the screen. We don't have it on our screens. I don't know if you have. Well, we've done what we should to have it on the screen, but we don't have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We don't have it yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my assistant is telling me that the usher has just said that we have a technical problem. We are really unlucky today, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The court deputy is checking. Do we have a problem?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Someone is coming to attend to the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, are you now able to see it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, this is another setback.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm addressing myself to the other people in the courtroom: Do you have the photograph displayed on your screens, or is it just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the witness has got the photograph on her screen. Perhaps we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can try. Yes, wonderful. We've got it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, as you can see, this is a photograph which you have already seen in this courtroom, and I would like you to indicate on this photograph, like you did on the previous photograph, I would like you to mark the route of the tramway, please.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it with the letter T? I think it should be a bit straighter, but anyway. Can you now indicate where Miljacka is, please. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And can you now tell me -- there are several high-rise buildings on these photographs. Tell me, which of the towers is the Unis building? Could you mark it with the letter U.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And the other high-rise which can you see on the left-hand side, could you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this one?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that one, too. Please tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a residential building. I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark with the letter B.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And now to the right-hand side of the Holiday Inn, which we're all familiar with, there is a high-rise building which is located between the Unis tower and this building here, which has a strange shape. Do you see which one I mean? Next to the Unis building, do you see that tower?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this one here?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right. What is that?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the former executive council building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you write in the letter G, which stands for "government."

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And the building which is in front of the government building?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this one?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's the same thing. It's connected to this other building. It was something or other about the executive council. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it with the letter G1, please.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And now can you see Vrbanja Most on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to get my bearings. It might be here. It's in this area, I think, but I can't remember specifically. It's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We can't see anything.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in this area somewhere, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Would you mark this bridge with the letter P.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is my next question: A while ago you said that the Miljacka river was like a borderline between the two warring factions. Do we still agree about this?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And everything else beyond that was territory controlled by the ABiH army, everything that lies above the line, the line which indicates where Miljacka is. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about the lines. I don't know what's behind this, for example, or what the lines were like exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to ask you to mark with an M where the Miljacka flows.

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But in your statement you did mention that the shots came from the territory which was controlled by the army of the Republika Srpska; is that right? So could I infer that you knew where the borders between the two factions were?

utterances.speaker: SABINA SABANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I have been telling you. The way we saw the situation, the Miljacka river was some sort of a relative border. But I can't tell you about anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have now concluded my cross-examination. I would like to thank the witness for her cooperation. Thank you. I apologise, I would like to offer this as evidence, as a Defence exhibit, and I would like the registrar to give me an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number D37.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: None, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Madam Witness, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness will be handled by my colleague, Mr. Waespi. May I be excused at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as we are concerned, with your leave I would just like to change seats, because the counsel next to me is going to cross-examine the witness, so it's easier for us to just change seats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think you need permission for that, but I'm happy to give it anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We can't hear counsel because he is not speaking into an open microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. I don't think we mentioned it, but the witness is Kemal Buco.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.
